title: Rethinking Prefetching for Intermittent Computing
problem: Conventional hardware prefetchers are energy-wasteful on batteryless energy harvesting systems (EHSs) because they aggressively fetch cache lines that are lost on power failure before any hit, wasting harvested energy. Frequent outages on EHSs mean that prefetched data that is never accessed before the next power loss represents pure energy overhead.
motivation: Batteryless IoT and edge devices powered by energy harvesting experience frequent outages, making energy efficiency the primary design constraint and rendering conventional prefetchers that optimize only for performance actively harmful.
method: IPEX (Intermittence-aware Prefetching EXtension) is an add-on layer that sits on top of existing prefetchers (hardware that tries to fetch data before it's needed) on batteryless energy-harvesting systems, without replacing them. It tracks which prefetched data blocks actually get used before power fails, then suppresses prefetching of blocks that historically go unused before the next outage (reducing 'useless prefetches'). It also monitors harvested energy levels to predict imminent power failures and, at that moment, throttles (reduces) how aggressively it prefetches, targeting only data blocks the processor is likely to use before power loss. This way, harvested energy is redirected from futile prefetches toward making actual progress on the program.
key_novelty: IPEX is the first prefetch extension that actively suppresses prefetches based on tracking data usage and predicting power failures, converting energy that would be wasted on cache lines never accessed into forward progress.
contributions: Identification and characterization of useless prefetches as a dominant energy-waste source in energy harvesting systems.
IPEX mechanism that integrates with any existing prefetcher to track and suppress prefetches that historically receive no hit before power failure.
Outage-aware prefetch-degree throttling that reduces prefetch aggressiveness just before predicted power loss.
Experimental demonstration of 7.86% average energy reduction (up to 21.64%) and 8.96% average performance improvement (up to 23.49%) over a conventional prefetcher.

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 7.86% avg energy reduction (up to 21.64%) vs conventional prefetcher

baselines: conventional prefetcher on EHS (unspecified baseline prefetcher)
limitations: Evaluation relies on simulation; real hardware prototype on an actual energy harvesting platform is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: energy-aware prefetch suppression for intermittent computing
